identifier: store currency
statement: The currency on your Shopify admin and that is displayed to your customers on your online store is your **store currency**.

identifier: payout currency
statement: The currency your deposits from Shopify Payments orders are made in is your **payout currency**.

identifier: Store currency
statement: This is the primary currency that your customers will use when making purchases on your store. You can select any currency from the available options in your store settings based on your customer base's location.

identifier: Payout currency
statement: The payout currency refers to the currency that Shopify Payments uses to deposit money into your bank account. This depends on the location of your store, and your bank account must generally be in the same country as your store.

identifier: Changing your store currency
statement: You can change the default currency displayed on your store to customers, even if this is not your local currency.

identifier: Impact of changing store currency
statement: * The currency of your product prices and discount rates update automatically, but not the amount. For example, if you change from USD to CAD, then a product that was listed as 20 USD is now listed as 20 CAD. * The amount and currency of shipping rates aren't updated automatically. * Gift cards with remaining balances in the old currency will no longer work. * Apps that have currency requirements different from the new currency won't work after the currency has been changed. * Changing your store currency might affect your reports, due to currency rate fluctuations and the report update cycles. * Changing your store currency might affect orders with pending payments. * Refunds processed after a currency change will also be affected by the currency change due to the difference in values. * If you use a payment provider other than Shopify Payments, then the currencies of all of your markets will update to match the new currency. * If you're using Paypal Express, then your new currency might not be supported. * Managed Markets is deactivated if you change your store currency. To continue using Managed Markets, your store currency must remain set to the required currency for your region.

identifier: Impact of changing store currency, Tip
statement: Your Shopify admin won't display a record of your product and discount prices in the previously assigned currency.

identifier: Settings > General > Store defaults > Currency display > Change store currency
statement: Only the store owner can change store currency. You can view and change your store currency from the **Store defaults** section of the [**General**](https://admin.shopify.com/settings/general) settings page.
note: Copy Q7-SH-K1936, from the account-setup page, says to contact Shopify Support to change the store currency after the first sale.

identifier: Changing your store currency
statement: * If you aren't using Shopify Payments, then [update your markets](/manual/markets/getting-started/managing-markets) when you change your store currency.

identifier: Selling and getting paid in different currencies
statement: The currency that your customers use to pay for their orders can be different from the currency of your payouts from Shopify Payments. That is, your store currency can be different from the currency of your bank account.

identifier: Supported payout currencies
statement: Your domestic currency is determined by your store location, and additional non-domestic currencies might be available depending on your Shopify plan.

identifier: Domestic currency
statement: Your domestic currency is determined by your Shopify Payments region and is the default currency for your payouts.

identifier: Currency conversion and exchange rates
statement: When a customer pays in a currency that's different from your payout currency, a currency exchange rate and conversion fee are applied at the time of payment capture. If you issue a refund, then the refund is processed at the current exchange rate, and no conversion fees are charged for refunds.

identifier: settings/payments
statement: In the [**Payments**](https://admin.shopify.com/settings/payments) section of your Shopify admin, you can track the current exchange rates and view historical exchange rates used for specific orders in the order's [timeline](/manual/fulfillment/managing-orders/managing-order-details#view-an-orders-timeline).

identifier: Adding payout currencies
statement: To receive payouts in an additional currency, you must have a [payout account](/manual/payments/shopify-payments/store-currency/payouts-in-multiple-currencies#add-multi-currency-bank) in that currency added to the [**Shopify Payments**](https://admin.shopify.com/settings/payments) section of your Shopify admin.

identifier: Adding payout currencies, Note
statement: If your store is based in the United States, then USD is always your default payout currency and can't be changed to another currency. You can add bank accounts in other supported currencies such as AUD, CAD, EUR, and GBP to receive secondary payouts in those currencies, but your primary payouts remain in USD.
scope: stores based in the United States

identifier: Multi-Currency Payouts, Plan requirements
statement: If your store is on a plan that doesn't support Multi-Currency Payouts, then you can still sell in multiple currencies, but all payouts are converted to your domestic currency.

identifier: Multi-Currency Payouts, Plan requirements
statement: If your store is on the Basic or Grow plan, and you're based in Canada, then you can choose USD as your default payout currency instead of CAD. A 1.5% payout fee applies.
scope: Basic or Grow plan, based in Canada

identifier: Multi-Currency Payouts, Additional requirements
statement: * You must have a business entity set up in a region that's eligible to use Multi-Currency Payouts. * You must have a bank account set up in a region that's [eligible to use Multi-Currency Payouts](#multi-currency-payouts-eligible-regions). * You must be listed as the store owner to activate Multi-Currency Payouts.
note: The first item of this list, on the plan, is in copy Q7-SH-K1636.

identifier: Add a bank account for Multi-Currency Payouts
statement: For Shopify Payments accounts in Singapore, Hong Kong, and the United Arab Emirates, payout accounts for non-domestic currencies must still be based in the store's domestic region.
scope: Shopify Payments accounts in Singapore, Hong Kong, and the United Arab Emirates

statement: 4. In the **Payout currency** section, select the currency of your bank.

identifier: Set a default bank account for payouts
statement: If you don't have a bank account set up in the currency that was used to pay for an order, then the payout is sent to your default bank account.

identifier: Replace a bank account
statement: You can't change the country or currency of the account that you want to add. The account that you want to add must be in the same currency as the account that you're replacing.

identifier: Delete currency
statement: Payouts are deposited into your default account if an account in that currency isn't added.

identifier: Handling orders in non-account currencies
statement: If you receive an order in a currency that you don't have a specific bank account for, then the funds are converted to your default account's currency.

identifier: Refunds in multiple currencies
statement: Refunds are processed in the same currency as the original order. The refund is deducted from the bank account in that currency. If you don't have a bank account in the original order's currency, then the refund is deducted from your default bank account in your domestic currency.

identifier: Chargebacks in multiple currencies
statement: Chargebacks are handled in the same currency as the original order. If a customer disputes a charge, then the chargeback amount is deducted from the bank account in that currency.

identifier: Refunds
statement: Refunds are always issued to a customer in the currency that they used to pay for the order.

identifier: Refunds
statement: * If the currency needs to be converted for the refund, then the current currency rate, and not the currency rate at the time of the order, is used in the conversion.

identifier: Guidelines and restrictions for selling in local currencies
statement: * Selling in local currencies is only supported by Adyen or Shopify Payments, which includes Shop Pay, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and PayPal in addition to the other Shopify Payments methods. Orders that are placed using other third-party payment providers are processed in your store's default currency.

identifier: Guidelines and restrictions for selling in local currencies
statement: * Some market pricing customizations, such as setting [product prices and percentage price adjustments](/manual/markets/customizations/catalogs) for each market, are available to all subscription plans and don't require Adyen or Shopify Payments.

identifier: Shopify POS
statement: [Shopify POS](/manual/sell-in-person) supports selling in a location's local currency only when you have a [business entity](/manual/your-account/business-entities) with Shopify Payments configured for that country.

identifier: Guidelines and restrictions for selling in local currencies
statement: * [Editing orders placed in international currencies](/manual/fulfillment/managing-orders/editing-orders/considerations#order-edit-currencies) is only available to some stores.

identifier: Guidelines and restrictions for selling in local currencies
statement: * You can view your reports only in your store currency.

identifier: Setting up currencies for markets, Note
statement: To process payments in multiple currencies, your store must use Shopify Payments or Adyen as its payment processor. If you use a different provider, then customers in all markets pay in your store's default currency.

identifier: currency customization
statement: Each market can have a currency customization that determines what currency is displayed to customers in that market. When a customer visits your store, their market is identified and prices are displayed in the currency configured for that market.

identifier: Currency inheritance
statement: [Submarkets](/manual/markets/getting-started/submarkets) inherit the currency customization of their parent market by default. If you add a currency customization to a submarket, then it overrides the parent's currency.

identifier: Markets > Currency > Dynamic / Manual
statement: * Select **Dynamic** to automatically convert prices. Prices are converted using the current market exchange rate, updated regularly. The currency conversion fee is included in the price that's displayed to your customer. * Select **Manual** to set a fixed exchange rate. The conversion fee isn't added to prices displayed to your customer. Instead, the fee is reflected in your payouts.

identifier: Currency for single-country markets
statement: When you create a market for a single country, the market's currency is automatically set to that country's local currency. For example, creating a Japan market automatically sets the currency to JPY. You can change this to any supported currency.

identifier: Currency for multi-country markets
statement: When you create a market with multiple countries, the default currency is set to your store's base currency, and local currencies are activated. This means each country in the market displays prices in its own local currency, automatically converted from the market's base currency.

identifier: Local currencies
statement: If you deactivate local currencies for a multi-country market, then prices in the market's base currency are displayed for all customers in that market, regardless of their location.

identifier: Fees and multi-entity stores
statement: If your store uses multiple business entities with Shopify Payments accounts in different countries, then the conversion fee depends on which entity processes the payment. If the customer's payment currency matches the entity's payout currency, then no conversion fee is charged.

identifier: Supported currencies
statement: Shopify Payments supports several currencies for international selling. The currencies available to you depend on your store's location and your payment processor. If a country's local currency isn't supported by Shopify Payments, then prices in the market's base currency are displayed to customers in that country instead.

identifier: Refunds in foreign currencies
statement: * **At the time of purchase**: The customer pays in their local currency. The payment is converted to your payout currency using the exchange rate at that time. * **At the time of refund**: You issue a refund in the customer's original currency. The refund amount is converted back to your payout currency using the exchange rate at that time.

identifier: Refunds with manual exchange rates
statement: If you use manual exchange rates, then refunds are still processed at the current market exchange rate at the time of the refund, not at the manual rate you set.

identifier: Chargebacks
statement: Chargebacks follow the same logic as refunds. The amount debited from your account in your payout currency is based on the exchange rate at the time of the chargeback, not the time of the original transaction.

identifier: PayPal multiple currencies
statement: When you sell in [multiple currencies through Shopify Payments](/manual/international/pricing), you can accept payments in various currencies using PayPal. This feature allows customers to pay for their orders using their preferred currency, with both PayPal and Shopify Checkouts displaying the transaction in the customer's selected currency. Refunds are also processed in the customer's currency.

If the currency matches one of Adyen's settlement currencies for the region, then payouts are settled in that currency accordingly.

identifier: draft orders, Note
statement: On draft orders that display a local currency other than your store currency, the foreign exchange rate is calculated when you create the draft order. This rate is fixed and used on the invoice regardless of whether the exchange rate changes. However, if you save the order as a draft and edit it afterwards, then pricing on the whole order is updated with the foreign exchange rate that's current at the time of the edit.

identifier: Orders > Drafts, Change the currency for a draft order
statement: You can manually override the local currency on a draft order from the default currency that displays based on the market or markets associated with a customer's region.

identifier: Changing the currency on draft orders in new Markets
statement: When no customer is assigned to a draft order, the order uses your store default values for currency and the backup region as the listed market.

identifier: Considerations for local currencies on draft orders
statement: However, the rate that Shopify Payments uses to calculate your payout is based on the market that's selected in Shopify. Therefore, the amount charged on the order can differ from the amount you receive in payment.

identifier: Check an order's currency
statement: If you're [selling in multiple currencies](/manual/international/pricing) and a customer's payment is processed in a local currency through a compatible payment provider, then the **Paid** section displays the amount paid in the customer's currency, also called the presentment currency. If the customer's payment is converted back to your store currency at checkout, then the order doesn't display as a multi-currency order.

identifier: Bulgaria currency change in Markets
statement: Bulgaria completed their changeover plan to transition from using the Bulgarian Lev (BGN) to the Euro (EUR) for electronic transactions on January 1, 2026.

identifier: Changes to Markets currency customizations with Bulgarian Lev
statement: If you use Shopify Payments, then your markets were previously configured to display and charge customers in Bulgarian Lev. This configuration has been changed to display and charge customers in Euros on your behalf.

identifier: Changes to store default currency and pricing with Bulgarian Lev
statement: Your store's default currency and product pricing aren't changed. If you don't use Shopify Payments, then you need to update your store default currency and product pricing to Euros. After you update your pricing and store default currency, you can't change it back to Bulgarian Lev.

identifier: Updates to gift cards and discounts with Bulgarian Lev
statement: When a customer redeems a gift card or discount in Bulgarian Lev on your store, then the redemption value or discount value is converted to Euros, or to the currency of their transaction. Fixed price discounts only exist in your store default currency.

identifier: Updates to catalogs in Bulgarian Lev
statement: If you previously created catalogs in Bulgarian Lev, then they're still valid and haven't been changed. After you update your catalog currency, you can't change it back to Bulgarian Lev.

identifier: Payments and payouts for Shopify Payments
statement: If you already had both EUR and BGN bank accounts linked to Shopify Payments, then we deactivated your BGN bank account and started using your EUR bank account for payouts. If you only had a BGN bank account linked to Shopify Payments, then we converted it to EUR and your payouts will continue to be deposited as expected.

identifier: Dual pricing display requirements with Bulgarian Lev
statement: Between August 8, 2025 and December 31, 2026, all businesses selling to customers in Bulgaria in Euros are required to display prices in both Euros and Bulgarian Lev. Transactions continue to take place in one currency.

identifier: business entity
statement: By default, all orders in your store are processed through your primary Shopify Payments account, which is associated with your store's home country. This is important for businesses that need to comply with local payment regulations, simplify tax reporting, or manage payouts in different currencies through local bank accounts.
